name: studybridge
description: For StudyBridge’s own content account only: Claude makes and checks lessons, practice questions, flashcards and practice papers for students studying on their own.
long_description: StudyBridge’s Owner uses this connector to make StudyBridge’s own content for students studying on their own: each subject’s syllabus, lessons, practice questions with hints and worked solutions, flashcards and original practice papers. Every question is checked a second time, in a new chat that never sees the answer, before students see it; anything that disagrees waits for the Owner in Admin → Content. It signs in only with StudyBridge’s content account. Tutors use Prof inside StudyBridge; students never use AI.

server_url.title: Server URL
server_url.description: From StudyBridge → Settings → Claude (your Supabase Project URL).

email.title: Content account email
email.description: The email of StudyBridge’s content account.

password.title: Content account password
password.description: Stored securely by Claude Desktop on this computer.

tools.name: list_library
tools.description: Files (for example a syllabus PDF) and lessons in the content account’s library.

tools.name: read_pdf
tools.description: Text of a PDF in the content account’s library.

tools.name: content_overview
tools.description: StudyBridge content: what each subject has so far.

tools.name: set_syllabus
tools.description: Set a subject’s topics in order.

tools.name: add_questions
tools.description: Practice questions with hints and worked solutions.

tools.name: questions_to_check
tools.description: Questions waiting for their second check, without answers.

tools.name: submit_checks
tools.description: Your own answers for the second check.

tools.name: confirm_checks
tools.description: Whether written answers mean the same as the key.

prompts.name: make_subject
prompts.description: Make StudyBridge content for a subject
prompts.text: Using StudyBridge’s content tools, help me make content for one subject. Start with content_overview and ask me which subject. Then: set its syllabus (the board’s topic names, in order, with codes and subtopics), write a lesson for each topic, about 10 practice questions per topic (mostly multiple choice and numbers, each with a hint and a worked solution), 10 flashcards per topic, and one original practice paper per paper of the real exam. Everything must be original: the same format, style and difficulty as the real exam, but never copied, reworded or adapted from a real past paper or a textbook.

prompts.name: check_waiting
prompts.description: Check waiting questions (in a new chat)
prompts.text: Using StudyBridge, check the questions waiting for their check. Call questions_to_check, solve every question yourself from scratch and carefully (don’t guess), and send your answers with submit_checks. If it asks you to compare written answers, say honestly with confirm_checks whether they mean the same. Repeat until nothing is waiting, then tell me how many passed and how many need me.
